entities.summary:
The Siege of Rome was a pivotal event in world history, occurring in 537–538 during the Gothic War of 535–554. It took place in the city of Rome, capital of the Western Roman Empire. The siege was a significant turning point in the conflict, marking a decisive victory for the Byzantine Empire under the leadership of Emperor Justinian I. The siege was led by the Gothic king Vitiges, who was ultimately defeated. The event had far-reaching consequences, shaping the trajectory of European history and influencing the rise of the Byzantine Empire.

The core events of the siege involved a prolonged assault on the city walls, which were eventually breached by the Byzantine forces. The city was under siege for several months, with both sides suffering significant losses. The siege ended on March 14, 538, with the defeat of the Goths and the capture of Rome.

The legacy of the Siege of Rome can be seen in the subsequent rise of the Byzantine Empire and its influence on the development of European politics, culture, and society. The event marked a significant shift in the balance of power in Europe, with the Byzantine Empire emerging as a dominant force.

In a final testament to its significance, the Siege of Rome can be seen as a precursor to the eventual fall of the Western Roman Empire, marking the end of an era in European history.
